text:
ConocoPhillips ticked up 0.34% today, extending a recovery from a sharp 2.9% drop on November 23rd when climate negotiations at COP31 collapsed without committing to phase out fossil fuels. The rebound suggests investors saw that failure as a mild positive for oil companies—no binding restrictions on oil and gas production emerged from the talks. Oil prices remain relatively stable, with US crude at $82.24 and global crude at $91.80 per barrel, providing a steady backdrop for energy stocks.

The stock has been volatile over the past two weeks, down 2% overall, which likely reflects the broader uncertainty around climate policy and geopolitical tensions in oil-producing regions (Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries and Middle East dynamics). That said, the company's heavy dividend yield continues to attract investors, as evidenced by recent analyst coverage highlighting energy stocks as attractive income plays during this period of elevated oil prices and policy uncertainty.
